mustFix.title: All three NT-5 coverageCommitments omit the pinned stage-coverage domain separator
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The subject declares coverageCommitment as sha256: || lowercase-hex(SHA-256(canonical-CBOR(CoverageV1.entries))). Each authored value reproduces exactly that raw, unprefixed canonical-CBOR hash.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: The pinned delivery.v2 wireSchema.commitments.domainRule states that each commitment is SHA-256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || deterministic-CBOR(value)), rendered as Sha256Text. The same closed commitments object assigns stageCoverage the domain opensip.ts-provider.stage-coverage.v1. CoverageV1.coverageCommitment is the required commitment over the stage entries array, so the stageCoverage domain applies. Independent RFC 8949 core-deterministic encodings reproduced the authored raw hashes, then produced different hashes after applying the required domain and NUL separator.
mustFix.counterexample: A conforming host recomputes a domain-separated stageCoverage commitment, rejects each frame for commitment mismatch, and never reaches the missing-key, unrequested-key, or unknown-to-complete comparison. All three records can therefore retain a host refusal while exercising none of the NT-5 property they are meant to isolate.
mustFix.impact: Every NT-5 fixture carries an independent earlier fault. The corpus is not a hostile-but-otherwise-well-formed implementation of EV-2 or EV-3, and its claim that the v1 coverageCommitment finding was landed is false.
mustFix.requiredRepair: In a successor, compute each value as sha256:hex(SHA-256(UTF8('opensip.ts-provider.stage-coverage.v1') || 0x00 || RFC-8949-core-deterministic-CBOR(entries))). Update all three fixture digests, catalog pins, recorded inputs, and construction text, then freeze and independently reproduce the successor bytes. Do not alter this frozen review subject in place.

decision: REJECT — 1 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. The v2 repairs reproduce the pinned FactCandidate delta, exact RequestedCoverageDomainV1 contexts, legal TypeScript-semantic keys, canonical key order, explicit unknown CoverageResultV1 baseline, fixture digests, custody, and authority boundaries. But every NT-5 coverageCommitment uses raw canonical-CBOR hashing instead of delivery.v2's closed opensip.ts-provider.stage-coverage.v1 domain-separated construction. A conforming host can therefore reject all three fixtures at commitment validation without exercising narrowing, widening, or unknown-to-covered refusal.
